label: KNOWLEDGE & RESEARCH
title: From questions to evidence.
description: A researcher, source reviewer and brief writer coordinate a referenced research brief.
problem: Teams need a clear research brief that distinguishes supported findings from open questions.
roles: Source reviewer: checks support and gaps
Brief writer: organises a referenced draft
output: A draft brief with source references, evidence gaps and review notes.
approval: A human reviewer verifies sources and approves the brief before it is shared.
permissions: Read access to the approved collection only. No publishing or external communications.
success: Every material finding can be traced to a supplied source, and unsupported claims are flagged.

label: PROCUREMENT & FINANCE
title: A clearer view of suppliers.
description: Bring contracts, spend and policy into one coordinated supplier review.
problem: Supplier decisions depend on evidence scattered across contracts, spend records and purchasing policy.
inputs: Approved supplier contracts and spend records
Internal procurement policy and review criteria
roles: Contract analyst: identifies terms and obligations
Spend analyst: summarises approved spend records
output: A draft supplier review with evidence references, policy exceptions and unresolved questions.
approval: Procurement or finance reviews the findings. The workflow cannot select suppliers or make purchases.
permissions: Read-only access to specifically approved contracts, spend data and policy documents.
success: Each finding names its evidence, and contract or policy exceptions are surfaced for human review.

label: PEOPLE & CUSTOMER TEAMS
title: Answers with the right context.
description: Support policy questions, onboarding and draft responses with approved knowledge.
problem: People and customer teams need consistent answers that respect access boundaries and current policy.
inputs: An approved policy or service knowledge collection
A user question and access scope
roles: Onboarding guide: structures the next steps
Response drafter: prepares a reviewable response
output: A cited answer or response draft grounded in approved knowledge.
approval: A responsible team member checks sensitive or consequential responses before sending.
permissions: Permission-aware reading of approved knowledge. No access to unrelated personnel or customer records.
success: Answers cite applicable sources, respect the user’s permissions, and flag missing or conflicting guidance.

label: FINANCIAL SERVICES
title: Diligence, organised.
description: Coordinate evidence collection and surface review findings for a human decision.
problem: Review teams need to organise a large diligence collection without losing the distinction between evidence and interpretation.
inputs: A review checklist and agreed scope
roles: Diligence coordinator: organises requests and evidence
Evidence reviewer: maps findings to the checklist
output: An evidence index, referenced review findings and an open-question register.
approval: A qualified reviewer decides what the evidence means. Investment and compliance decisions remain human-owned.
permissions: Read-only access within a defined diligence workspace; no trading or transaction execution.
success: Each checklist item is linked to evidence or explicitly marked as unresolved.

label: INDUSTRIAL & ENERGY
title: Asset knowledge, put to work.
description: Turn manuals and maintenance knowledge into referenced planning support.
problem: Maintenance planners need relevant asset information and clear documentation gaps before making a plan.
inputs: Asset context and a planning question
output: A referenced planning draft with assumptions, dependencies and missing documentation.
approval: An authorised engineer reviews the draft. Equipment operation and maintenance authorisation stay with qualified people.
permissions: Read-only approved documentation. No access to operational control systems.
success: Planning considerations cite applicable documentation, and missing safety or operating information is flagged.

label: TECHNOLOGY & TELECOM
title: Understand the incident.
description: Investigate incidents, review changes and assess capacity through a focused workflow pack.
problem: Technology teams need an evidence-based picture of an incident, change or capacity constraint.
inputs: Approved incident reports, change records and runbooks
An investigation scope and relevant capacity data
roles: Change reviewer: compares changes to policy
Capacity analyst: examines supplied capacity evidence
output: A referenced analysis draft with observations, hypotheses and questions for operators.
approval: An operator reviews the evidence. The workflow cannot change systems or apply remediations.
permissions: Read-only approved records; operational actions require a separately authorised scope.
success: Observations are separated from hypotheses, and recommendations cite the evidence that supports them.
